subject: MSA redline call & onboarding prep — Hemera Therapeutics

Cc: procurement@hemera.com, Danielle Brooks <danielle@bryantlaw.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MSA redlines & onboarding check-in

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our legal and procurement teams finished an initial pass on the MSA and have a set of redlines they'd like to review together. Would Redwood be available for a 45–60 minute redline scrub to walk through the changes and close open terms (data residency, audit rights, termination for convenience)? We also want to confirm the onboarding checklist (SAML SSO, logging retention, evidence for SOC2).

Open windows this week: Wed 12/2 10–12 PT, Thu 12/3 13–16 PT, Mon 12/7 morning PT. If none of those work we can push to early next week.

I've attached the redline file and a short evidence manifest. Danielle (cc) is our outside counsel and will join for the legal items.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Procurement
Hemera Therapeutics

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the materials. We can absolutely run a redline scrub. My team is booked in the windows you listed but I can carve out time. Proposed slots (PT):
- Thu 12/3 14:00–15:00 PT — primary proposal
- Mon 12/7 09:00–10:00 PT — backup

Agenda I suggest: (1) Legal redline walk (Danielle + Hemera counsel), (2) Data residency & retention specifics, (3) SSO/systems evidence and owners, (4) Rollout timeline & next steps. I've attached a short proposed agenda.

Marissa will own the onboarding evidence handoff; Rishi will join for SLA/latency and routing fallbacks. Jordan will take notes and follow up on action items. If Danielle or Hemera prefer a longer session we can extend to 75 minutes.

Best,

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@hemera.com>

Cc: procurement@hemera.com, Danielle Brooks <danielle@bryantlaw.com>

Kimberly —

Thanks — Thu 12/3 at 14:00 PT won't work on our side (internal conflict). Can we move to Mon 12/7 09:00–10:15 PT? That gives Danielle extra time. If you can commit Marissa and Rishi for the full 75 minutes, that would be ideal.

Top 3 blocker clauses (high level):
1) Audit & access scope — Hemera needs clarity on how audit logs are stored and what extracts are available.
2) Data residency & subcontractors — we need explicit commitments if data leaves region.
3) Termination & data return — timing and export format guarantees.

We uploaded a cleaned redline (MSA_redlines_Hemera_v3.docx) to the Drive link; please pull before the meeting.

—Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Procurement, Hemera Therapeutics
